Problem Statement:
In the Intelligent Health Claims Management System, claim processing was slow due to tightly coupled services, high database load, and delays in handling large volumes of healthcare claim transactions. Users experienced longer response times, which affected operational efficiency.

My Role:
As a Java Full Stack Developer, I was responsible for designing and developing Spring Boot microservices, implementing Apache Kafka for asynchronous event processing, integrating Redis caching, and building Angular-based user interfaces. I also worked on MongoDB schema optimization, REST API development, and deployment using Docker and AWS EC2.

Solution & Impact:

Developed and maintained 10+ Spring Boot microservices to improve scalability and maintainability.
Implemented Apache Kafka for real-time event-driven communication between services.
Introduced Redis caching and optimized MongoDB indexing strategies.
Built responsive Angular modules to streamline claim management workflows.
Collaborated with QA, business analysts, and DevOps teams in Agile sprints.

Result:

Reduced application response time by 30%.
Improved user task completion speed by 20%.
Enhanced system scalability to handle 1M+ claim records efficiently.
Increased overall reliability and maintainability of the platform, enabling faster claim processing and better user experience.
